title: Spot virtual machines and eviction policy

videos.script: Azure has machines nobody is using right now. It will rent them to you for much less. {{offer}} The catch fits in one sentence. When Azure needs the capacity back, it takes the machine, with thirty seconds' notice at most. {{evict}} That sounds like a reason to stay away. For a lot of work it is not. A nightly report that saves its progress, a worker reading a queue, a build that can run again: each can lose a machine and carry on. {{fits}} This lesson starts with what Spot sells, and with the one word that makes a machine Spot. You will write it in Bicep, and see that the compiler takes any spelling of it. {{policy}} Then the two reasons for an eviction, and the two things it can leave behind. One of them keeps billing you for disks. {{notice}} Then the notice itself. A program on the machine has to ask for it, every second, and you will read one that does. {{mix}} Last, a scale set with a floor of regular machines and Spot above it. And the arithmetic that decides what belongs on Spot. Not how important the work is. What one eviction would cost.
